verified_claims: Step 1: gcd(m,a_i)>1 for all i<=n iff P(m) hits every minimal member of F_n, so a_{n+1}=min(V_n cap (a_n,inf)); reduction checked.
Step 2: V_n is the union over tau in b(M_n) of the multiples of prod(tau), and minimal transversals use only primes of union(M_n); checked (finite descending to a minimal transversal).

Step 3: V_{n+1} subseteq V_n (members are removed only when the new S=P(a_{n+1}) satisfies S subsetneq M, and valid m hits S); given stabilization at M, every P(a_j) contains an M-member (work in F_{max(j,N)}), V subseteq V_n for all n, and every term a_n lies in V (pairwise gcd>1); hence a_{n+1}=min(V cap (a_n,inf)) and the sequence is exactly the increasing enumeration of V cap [a_1,inf).

Step 4: V is a union of residue classes mod L=prod(U); an L-periodic set's increasing enumeration b_n satisfies b_{n+T}=b_n+L with T=|V cap [1,L]|>=1; since a_1 in V, the shift gives a_{n+T}=a_n+L for EVERY n>=1. Numerically confirmed for a_1=15 (L=30, T=8, a_9=45=a_1+30).

Step 6: fixed point iff b(M) subseteq M iff b(M)=M; all three implications re-derived, including the defect-realization argument for (i)=>(ii) (a defect tau would be realized as a term prod(tau)*p^j, forcing a change).

Step 7: at an essential-prime entry the minimal sub-transversal tau* of P(a_j) is a defect, q divides k=a_j/D, and every multiple of D is valid, giving the exact identity a_j=D*(floor(a_{j-1}/D)+1); derived and matched on three entry events (a_1=15: k=6=floor(15/3)+1; a_1=30: k=16; a_1=105: k=11 at j=3 and k=13 at j=8).
Lemma A (TERM): any m in V_n with a_1<=m<=a_n is a term; proof correct and uses only the unconditional monotonicity V_i superseteq V_n.
Lemma B: consecutive S-smooth numbers satisfy n_{i+1} <= (min S) n_i; correct, and the 'smallest smooth exceeding X' consequence holds since 1 is S-smooth.
Lemma C: B_n nonempty implies B_{n+1} nonempty; full case split (S not subseteq tau*, S subseteq tau* added, S subseteq tau* not added) independently checked, including the M'' survival subcase.

CB (Step 9): assuming k>a_1 gives a_{j-1}>=a_1 D; the constructed m=Dc (c = least tau*-smooth number > a_1/D, or m=D when D>a_1) satisfies P(m)=tau*, a_1<m<=a_{j-1}, m in V_{j-1}; hence m=a_s with s>=2; B_{j-1}=empty (tau* is a defect, any member subseteq tau* would contradict minimality or defectness) back-propagates via Lemma C contrapositive to B_{s-1}=empty, forcing tau* in M_s and B_s nonempty, which forward-propagates to B_{j-1} nonempty — contradiction. Verified in full, including edge cases D>a_1 and s=j-1.

Consequence chain: every essential prime divides some cofactor k<=a_1 (primes of a_1 trivially <=a_1), so all antichains live over the finite set {p<=a_1}; a change of M_n strictly shrinks V_n (injectivity of the M-to-V map — independently supplied the standard CRT recovery of b(M) from V), so M_n never repeats, takes finitely many values, and stabilizes; Steps 3-4 then deliver the theorem.

End-to-end hand simulations for a_1 in {2,6,15,30,105} agree with the theory (e.g., a_1=105 evolves through the identity-(4) entries k=11,13 and stabilizes at the self-dual antichain {{2,3},{2,5},{2,7},{3,5,7}} with L=210; the a_1=2310 collapse mechanism confirmed: a_n+1 is always coprime to a_n while a_n+2 stays valid, so terms are consecutive even numbers until a power of 2 collapses M to {{2}}).
summary: Complete and correct proof. Steps 1-4 soundly reduce the problem to the increasing enumeration of a blocker-defined valid set once the minimal-support antichain M_n stabilizes, and the genuine crux — finiteness of essential primes — is resolved by the Cofactor Bound via a correct contradiction combining the TERM lemma, the smooth-gap bound, and bidirectional persistence of sub-members of the realized defect (Lemma C). I re-derived every load-bearing step and hand-checked small cases; no counterexample, circularity (Lemma A uses only the unconditional part of Step 3), hidden quantifier change, or degenerate-case failure found; the conclusion holds for every n>=1 because a_1 itself is valid. Minor expository issues only, none fatal: Steps 3-4 speak of M_infinity before stabilization is proved (logically closed in Step 8), the injectivity 'V determines M' behind the no-repeat count in Step 8 is only sketched (the standard CRT recovery fills it), and the blocker involution b(b(M))=M is cited without proof (elementary). The extensive 'computationally verified, 0 failures' claims were not re-run, but they corroborate lemmas that are fully proved in the text and are not load-bearing.
transfer_assessment: Reusable: encode pairwise-gcd constraints as a clutter of prime supports; validity = being a transversal of the minimal-support antichain; valid sets decrease monotonically, and once the antichain stabilizes the greedy sequence equals the increasing enumeration of a finite union of divisibility classes, which is periodic and yields a_{n+T}=a_n+L from n=1 (key: a_1 itself is valid).
Reusable: cofactor identity a_j = D*(floor(a_{j-1}/D)+1) whenever the next term realizes a defect transversal with radical D — converts new-prime-entry events into a numeric bound on the cofactor.

Reusable: TERM lemma (every valid integer in [a_1,a_n] is already a term) plus a smooth-number gap bound to manufacture a term with prescribed prime support — a clean template for turning size bounds into structural contradictions in greedy divisor sequences.
Reusable: forward-persistence of sub-members of a fixed set under antichain updates (Lemma C), applied both directly and contrapositively to propagate emptiness/nonemptiness across time.

Caution (mildly misleading presentation): the heavy 'computationally verified, 0 failures' rhetoric is redundant for lemmas that are in fact proved, and could mislead a reader about which statements are load-bearing; a final writeup should also reorder (M_infinity is used before stabilization is shown) and prove the blocker involution and the V-to-M recovery explicitly.

Correctly refuted routes worth remembering: essential primes need not be <= max P(a_1) (only <= a_1, e.g. 385 -> 19); |M_n| is not monotone (it can grow large then collapse to {{2}}, as for a_1=2310 once a power of 2 appears as a term).
